 JUDGMENT  Aggrieved by the award passed in M.V.C.No.129/2016 and M.V.C.No.130/2016 dated Smt. Kunnilakshmi vs Divisional Controller Ksrtc on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34674923/

sentences.text:
In M.V.C.No.129/2016,
the claimants have claimed compensation of an amount of Rs.25,70,000/- and in M.V.C.No.130/2016, the claimants have claimed compensation of an amount of Rs.32,50,000/-.

2. The case of the claimants is that on 10.07.2016, at about 2:20 p.m., both the claimants were proceeding on a motor cycle on the left side of the road, at that time, NC: 2023:KHC:41478 the driver of the KSRTC Bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle.
As a result, both the claimants fell down and sustained injuries.
The claimants in M.V.C.No.129/2016 are the parents and the claimants in M.V.C.No.130/2016 are the wife, children and mother of the deceased.

In MFA No.3930/2018 arising out of M.V.C.No.129/2016 :-
3.
The case of the claimants in M.V.C.No.129/2016 is that the deceased was 36 years old earning an amount of Rs.800/- to Rs.1,000/- per day.
The Court below as there was no evidence, had taken an amount of Rs.6,000/- as the income and granted an amount of Rs.5,40,000/- towards loss of dependency.

Towards funeral expenses an amount of Rs.15,000/-, towards medical expenses an amount of Rs.2,70,000/-, towards transportation charges an amount of Rs.10,000/- and towards loss of love and affection an amount of NC: 2023:KHC:41478
Rs.40,000/- was granted.

Altogether,
compensation of an amount of Rs.8,75,000/- was granted.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant submits that he was working as a mechanic and earning an amount of Rs.800/- to Rs.1,000/- per day.
The claimant has examined the owner of the mechanical shop.
Learned counsel submits that the Court below ought not to have taken an amount of Rs.6,000/- as the income per month.
It is submitted that the compensation granted by the Tribunal was not just and reasonable.

5. Learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company submits that as there was no reasonable evidence, the Tribunal had taken the income at Rs.6,000/- per month and rightly granted compensation and no grounds are made out seeking enhancement of the compensation.
NC: 2023:KHC:41478 6.
Having heard the learned counsel on either side, perused the entire material on record.
In this case, according to the claimant he was earning an amount of Rs.800/- to Rs.1,000/- per day and he has also examined the owner of the mechanic shop.
Except giving the oral evidence, no other documents are marked on their behalf and the Court below had taken the income of the claimant at Rs.6,000/- per month.

As this is an accident of the year 2016, as per the chart notional income is an amount of Rs.9,500/-, whereas in this case, the claimant is a mechanic which is a skilled job, this Court is inclined to take an amount of Rs.10,000/- as the income and as he is 36 years old, future prospects would be 40% i.e., Rs.4,000/- and the income would be Rs.10,000+Rs.4,000 =
Rs.14,000/-.
As he is a bachelor, 50% has to be deducted towards personal expenses.
His contribution to the family would be an amount of Rs.7,000x12 and the relevant multiplier is 15.
Hence, loss of dependency would come to Rs.7000x12x15 = Rs.12,60,000/-.
As both the claimants are parents, towards consortium, an NC: 2023:KHC:41478 amount of Rs.88,000/- is granted.

Altogether the claimants are eight in number and 1/5th has to be deducted towards personal expenses i.e., Rs.2,660/-.
